sn10.7:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
sn10.7:1.2: Now on that occasion the Blessed One was instructing, exhorting, inspiring, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk concerning Nibbāna.
sn10.7:1.3: And those bhikkhus were listening to the Dhamma with eager ears, attending to it as a matter of vital concern, applying their whole mind to it.
sn10.7:1.4: Then the female yakkha Punabbasu’s Mother hushed her little children thus:
sn10.7:2.4: I wish to listen to the Dhamma of the Teacher,
sn10.7:3.1: “When the Blessed One speaks of Nibbāna,
sn10.7:4.1: “In the world one’s own son is dear,
sn10.7:4.2: In the world one’s own husband is dear;
sn10.7:4.3: But even dearer than them for me
sn10.7:4.4: is the quest for this Dhamma
sn10.7:5.1: “For neither one’s own son nor husband,
sn10.7:5.2: Though dear, can release one from suffering
sn10.7:5.3: As listening to true Dhamma frees one
sn10.7:5.4: From the suffering of living beings.
sn10.7:6.3: For freedom from aging and death.
sn10.7:6.5: I wish to listen to the Dhamma
sn10.7:7.3: Pay attention only to the Dhamma,
sn10.7:7.4: For listening to true Dhamma is pleasant.
sn10.7:7.5: Because we have not known true Dhamma
sn10.7:8.2: Bewildered. He is the maker of light
sn10.7:8.4: The One with Vision teaches the Dhamma.
sn10.7:9.1: “It is good that my son has become so wise,
sn10.7:9.2: He whom I bore and nursed at my breast.
sn10.7:9.3: My son, Of the Supremely Enlightened One,
sn10.7:10.2: Today I have emerged at last.
